name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,790

clue.text: One upright, holy man with tablets (7)

blocks.note: ST = saint
with = and
E = ecstasy, a tablet; two of them

explanation.surface: A saint stands tall, carrying stone tablets like Moses coming down the mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tablets' suggests the Ten Commandments, but it is the drug slang: E is an ecstasy pill, so tablets are EE.
explanation.definitionFit: A standee is someone who stands, for instance a passenger without a seat: one upright.

clue.text: Conflict involving close contact between big Japanese corporations (4)

definitions.text: Conflict involving close contact between big Japanese corporations

blocks.note: reads as a bitter business rivalry; the setter means a bout where two bodies press together
reads as large Japanese firms; corporation is also old slang for a big belly

explanation.surface: A business-page story about a close-fought feud among Japan's big companies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporations' reads as companies, but it is also an old joke word for a paunch: sumo is a clash of big Japanese bellies.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is Japanese wrestling between very heavy men who push against each other body to body.

clue.text: All complainants initially taking oaths, right to drop charges (7)

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word gives its first letter
to drop is to let fall, so right, R, falls out of the word

blocks.note: first letters of All and Complainants
oaths = CURSES, without R (right)

explanation.surface: In court, the plaintiffs are swearing furiously, and the prosecutor withdraws the charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' looks like a noun at the end of a legal story, but it is the verb: she charges him = she accuses him.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the legal sense: to charge someone with a crime is to accuse them of it.

clue.text: It's one boring routine (5)

blocks.note: a tool that bores holes
a practised routine, as in a fire practice

explanation.surface: Someone sighs that the daily routine is tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' reads as dull, which matches 'routine', but here it means making holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill is a tool that bores; a drill is also a practised routine.

clue.text: Cosmetic change finally applied to the old boat (8)

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so the word gives its last letter

blocks.note: last letter of change
ye = an old spelling of the
an ocean liner

explanation.surface: A cosmetic makeover is given to an old boat, a lick of paint at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cosmetic' seems to describe the change to the boat, but it is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: eyeliner is one cosmetic, drawn along the edge of the eyelids.

clue.text: Adorn sculpture of stone (7)

indicators.note: a sculpture is a reshaping of the material, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: Decorate the place with a stone sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of stone' looks like it describes the sculpture, but those words are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to festoon something is to hang garlands and chains of decoration over it.

clue.text: Pull up fish beneath Fal's banks - caught using this? (3,3)

indicators.note: in a down entry, pulling up turns the word upward
the banks of a river are its edges, so the word gives its outside letters
in a down entry, the fish goes under the first piece

blocks.note: outer letters of Fal
a dory is a sea fish; reversed upward

explanation.surface: An angler hauls a fish out of the River Fal and wonders what tackle landed it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a river in Cornwall. The question mark marks the definition as a hint rather than a synonym: the fish was caught using a fly rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly rod is the fishing rod used for fly-fishing, so the fish might well be caught using this.

clue.text: Arranges A team's reserves (4,5)

blocks.note: sets = arranges, as in sets a table
A as printed
a team is a side

explanation.surface: A manager picks the first team's substitutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserves' looks like the noun for a team's substitutes, but it is the verb: she reserves it = she sets it aside.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to set something aside is to keep it back for later, to reserve it.

clue.text: Early on, moves on board to generate opportunity (7)

blocks.note: the first moves of a chess game have a name of their own
a chance or gap to exploit

explanation.surface: A chess player makes early moves that create a chance to attack.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a description, not a synonym: the early moves on a chessboard are the opening.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening is both the first phase of a chess game and an opportunity.

clue.text: One day going over country's proposal (10)

indicators.note: going over is turning over, so the pair turns round, bottom to top in a down entry

blocks.note: I = one
Mon = Monday
a country is a nation

explanation.surface: One day a nation's proposal is considered in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going over' could apply to the whole phrase, but only the first two pieces turn round; the country follows as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a nomination is a proposal of someone for a post or award.

clue.text: Appliances generally - can openers for cheap hotels in Eire oddly being included (9)

indicators.note: the openers of words are the letters that open them, their first letters
oddly means taking the odd-numbered letters
the other letters are included, put inside, the word for can

blocks.note: can = may, be allowed to; this is the outer word
first letters of cheap and hotels
IN as printed
the first and third letters of Eire

explanation.surface: Kitchen gadgets: tin openers supplied to budget Irish hotels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can openers' looks like the tin gadget, but 'can' is the verb meaning be allowed to, and 'openers for' belongs with the words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Machinery is the collective noun: machines or appliances taken as a whole, hence 'generally'.

clue.text: Measure rather more covers (5)

indicators.note: the phrase covers, holds inside it, the answer

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of rather into the start of more

explanation.surface: A measure that's rather more generous covers more.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the gap between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a therm is a unit measuring heat, used on British gas bills.

clue.text: Playing finale, soloist's state of personal withdrawal (4-9)

indicators.note: the letters are played around with

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

explanation.surface: A soloist plays the finale alone, lost in a private world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' suits the soloist on stage, which hides that it is telling you to rearrange the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-isolation is withdrawing yourself from contact with others, as in the pandemic.

clue.text: Take tour of sugar producers, possibly, in river islands (10)

indicators.note: the sugar producers go in the river

blocks.note: to do a country is to tour it
the Dee, a British river; the outer piece
sugar canes, the plants that produce it

explanation.surface: A tourist visits sugar plantations along a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' is fair because sugar also comes from beet. The Dee is a river in Scotland and another between England and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dodecanese are a group of Greek islands in the Aegean, Rhodes the largest.

clue.text: Preoccupied and shaken, lacking time to overcome brain disease (8)

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the word for shaken goes without its T
to overcome is to come over, so the letters for shaken close over the disease

blocks.note: shaken = TOSSED, without T (time); the outer piece
BSE, mad cow disease, which attacks the brain

explanation.surface: Someone distracted and shaken, fearing a brain illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overcome' here means covering over, not defeating.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone obsessed has a mind preoccupied, fixed on one thing.

clue.text: Pie that's hashed with last of egg pasta (9)

indicators.note: to make a hash of something is to mess it up
takes the last letter of egg

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters
last letter of egg

explanation.surface: A pie that has been chopped into hash, with the dregs of an egg and some pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hashed' is a cooking word in a food clue, so it passes as part of the recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: spaghetti is one kind of pasta, the long thin strings.

clue.text: With fiddle, uncapped device (6)

indicators.note: the cap, the first letter, comes off

blocks.note: w = with, a standard abbreviation
fiddle = FIDGET, without its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone fiddles about with a gadget that has lost its lid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncapped device' reads as one phrase, but 'uncapped' belongs with fiddle and 'device' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for any small gadget whose proper name you don't know.

clue.text: Yorkshire batter finally scores, bagging a 6 (8)

definitions.note: 6 is a cross-reference to 6 down, SETS ASIDE, used as the verb 'reserves'

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so each word gives its last letter
to bag something is to put it in a bag, so the outer letters hold the A inside

blocks.note: last letters of Yorkshire and batter; the outer piece
A as printed
scores = marks, as in a test

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire cricketer finally gets off the mark, hitting a six.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket scene makes '6' look like a six hit over the boundary; it points to 6 down, whose answer SETS ASIDE is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark something is to set it aside for a particular purpose.

clue.text: Prophet's revered bone, maybe, uncovered on return pilgrimage (6)

indicators.note: with its covers off, the word loses its first and last letters
to return is to go back, so the pilgrimage reads backwards

blocks.note: a revered bone might be a RELIC; without its outer letters
the hajj is the Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca, also spelt haj

explanation.surface: A prophet's holy relic is unveiled when pilgrims come home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks the bone as one example of a relic, a saint's remains kept for veneration.
explanation.definitionFit: Elijah is one of the major prophets of the Old Testament, taken up to heaven in a chariot of fire.

clue.text: Expected to catch cold, being lean (7)

indicators.note: the phrase catches the letter, holding it inside

blocks.note: in line (with forecasts) = expected; the outer piece
C = cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone thin enough that they were always likely to catch a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lean' reads as the adjective thin, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: a tower that inclines leans, as the one at Pisa does.

clue.text: A bloke runs riot on Circle Line (8)

indicators.note: the letters run riot, out of order
the rearranged letters sit on, next to, the circle

blocks.note: A BLOKE plus R (runs, from cricket scoring); anagram fodder
a circle is the shape of O

explanation.surface: A man causes trouble on the Circle Line of the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle is a London Underground line, so 'Circle Line' reads as one name. It splits: Circle is a letter and Line is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bakerloo, named from Baker Street and Waterloo, is one of the lines on the London Underground.

clue.text: Rock singer? (7)

blocks.note: reads as the music genre; the setter means a crag on a riverbank
reads as a vocalist; the setter means a legendary siren who sang to boatmen

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock singer' suggests a rock-music vocalist; the Lorelei is the siren of German legend who sat on a rock above the Rhine and lured boatmen to their deaths with her song.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is both a rock on the Rhine and the singing siren said to live there.

clue.text: When ordered, please pass by (6)

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters

explanation.surface: A polite instruction: when told to, please walk past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Please pass by' reads as a polite request, but please is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym used of time: hours that elapse pass by.

clue.text: One gauging strength of, e.g., rum hotel served up with more Cola (13)

definitions.text: One gauging strength of, e.g., rum

indicators.note: the letters are served up mixed, like a cocktail

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder; 13 letters in all

explanation.surface: A hotel bar serves rum and Coke, heavy on the cola, and someone checks how strong it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs up to 'rum', so 'hotel' belongs to the wordplay even though it reads as part of the drinking scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcoholometer measures the alcohol content, the strength, of a spirit such as rum.

clue.text: Article on old army character from abroad (5)

blocks.note: the definite article
Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve; 'old' because it was renamed the Army Reserve in 2014

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a veteran soldier who is a foreign character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' reads as a person, but it is a letter of an alphabet, here Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a character from abroad.

clue.text: Some fallen idol rises a god (4)

indicators.note: some of the phrase is taken
in a down entry, rising reads the letters bottom to top

blocks.note: the last letter of fallen and the first three of idol, then read upward

explanation.surface: A fallen idol rises again to become a god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fallen' and 'rises' seem to contrast in the surface, but only 'rises' has a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief god of Norse mythology.

clue.text: Be first to succeed former partner (5)

indicators.note: to succeed is to come after, so first follows the former partner

blocks.note: an ex
1st written with I for 1

explanation.surface: Advice to a rival: beat your ex to success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be first' reads as a phrase, but 'Be' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'I think, therefore I am' is about existing, the most basic sense of the verb be.

clue.text: Wrapped up leper clad in shreds (9)

indicators.note: the letters are torn to pieces and rebuilt

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A leper dressed in rags, bundled up.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture of a leper in rags hides that 'in shreds' tells you to tear up the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something parcelled has been made into a parcel, wrapped up in paper.

clue.text: One-time recluse to return, revealing himself (7)

definitions.text: One-time recluse to return, revealing himself

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the letters are read backwards
the recluse shows himself inside the clue's own words

blocks.note: the last letter of one, all of time and the first two of recluse, then read backwards

explanation.surface: A hermit comes back into the world and shows his face.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter reuses the definition on purpose: the recluse reveals himself hidden backwards in the very words that define him. 'One-time' fits because eremite is an old word.
explanation.definitionFit: Eremite is an archaic word for a hermit, so a one-time word for a recluse.

clue.text: Formally confirm Top comeback for one-time circus performer (3,4)

indicators.note: a comeback is a coming back, so the letters come back, reading backwards

blocks.note: to seal a deal is to confirm it formally
top = No. 1, written NO I; reversed

explanation.surface: A former circus star is officially confirmed for a comeback show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-time' is fair because performing sea lions have largely left the circus.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea lions were trained to balance balls on their noses in circus acts.
